description: DK-Mem distinction lexicon v2 (DRAFT, not frozen): the 15 pilot-reviewed Hindi entries of v1, unchanged, plus 18 Marathi (mr) and Gujarati (gu) kinship/register entries from the Member-3 proposal with their surface forms unchanged. The mr/gu entries were reviewed by the model (Claude), NOT by native speakers: no human verification was available. Each mr/gu entry's notes carry its review verdict; 'unsure' entries are kept and their risks are stated. Still held, as in the proposal: Gujarati naani (homograph of the adjective 'small/young') and Marathi naani, so a daadi/naani pair is tagged on one side only and the gate cannot veto it; Marathi periphrases (babanchi aai / aaichi aai) are not tagged. Built by tools/build_lexicon_v2.py; v1 is unchanged.

NEW, UNVALIDATED. Molesworth (p.64) glosses आजी as 'a grandmother paternal or maternal', i.e. lineage-NEUTRAL - this contradicts MEMBER3_COORDINATION.md ('paternal grandmother'). Value is therefore 'aaji', not 'dadi'. CONSEQUENCE: an aaji/nani mismatch across two mentions would make the gate return 'incompatible' even if both refer to the same maternal grandmother - raised with Member 2. Molesworth also lists आजी as a respectful particle of address. Regex: closed list of agglutinated postpositions (anchored, so आजीवन 'lifelong' does NOT match); suffix list needs native review. || MODEL REVIEW (Claude, not native-verified): unsure. [Claude draft, not native-verified] Lineage-neutral value 'aaji' is a sound choice, but a mismatch with nani-type terms is then not detected and aaji is also an address term for any elderly woman. Class kinship fine; regex anchoring is correct (आजीवन excluded). Suffix list lacks common forms: neuter possessive -चं (e.g. आजीचं), -कडून, -साठी, -सोबत/-बरोबर, -पासून, -वर; romanised inflected forms (aajichi, kakanna) are not covered either. NATIVE DECISION REQUIRED before activation: keep gating, restrict, or drop this entry; any suffix additions listed above are unconfirmed proposals. Entry stays PROVISIONAL (lexicon_v2 overlay only, not in v1).

NEW, UNVALIDATED. Least-formal singular 2nd person (Wiktionary). Dative tula/तुला; possessive तुझा/तुझी/तुझे/तुझं/तुझ्या. RISK: तुला also a noun (balance/Libra) - unverified, low. Gap: emphatic clitics (तूच) not covered. Held: romanized possessives (tujha/tuza - inconsistent romanization). || MODEL REVIEW (Claude, not native-verified): ok. [Claude draft, not native-verified] तू (informal singular) with dative/possessive forms is correct as a closed exact-word list. Gaps: agglutinated postposition forms (तुझ्याशी, तुझ्याकडे, तुझ्यावर), emphatic तूच/तुलाच/तुझंच, and romanised possessives (already noted). तुला as 'balance' is rare.

NEW, UNVALIDATED. Mid-formality 2nd person AND 2nd person plural (Wiktionary) - a tu/tumhi difference may reflect number, not register. EXCLUDED: आपण (Molesworth: reflexive pronoun 'standing indifferently for I, thou, he, we, ye, they'; also inclusive 'we'). || MODEL REVIEW (Claude, not native-verified): unsure. [Claude draft, not native-verified] तुम्ही is both polite singular and plural 'you', so a tu/tumhi difference may reflect number, not register (as noted); आपण is a further formal 'you' but is excluded for ambiguity, so formality is only partly covered. Also note: under README convention 2 same-vocative tu/tumhi pairs are gold-same, but the gate treats tu vs tumhi as incompatible and would veto the merge - a design consequence worth stating. Missing forms: तुम्हास, तुम्हाशी, तुमच्याशी/तुमच्याकडे, तुमचंच. NATIVE DECISION REQUIRED before activation: keep gating, restrict, or drop this entry; any suffix additions listed above are unconfirmed proposals. Entry stays PROVISIONAL (lexicon_v2 overlay only, not in v1).

[Claude draft, not native-verified] Father's mother is right for Gujarati dadi (unlike lineage-neutral Marathi aaji). Gap: the very common Gujarati term 'ba' (also used for mother) is not included, deliberately or not; it is ambiguous, so leaving it out is the safer choice. Gaps: romanised inflected forms (e.g. -ne/-no/-ni attached in Latin script) are not covered; separate-word postpositions are fine because the matcher is per token.
